questions.q: Why does this lesson say current-state landscape analysis should come before designing the target state?
options: Because stakeholders enjoy reviewing inventories more than designs
Because a target-state design that doesn't account for what already exists is a wish list, not a design
Because Salesforce requires a documented current state before any org can be provisioned
Because current-state analysis is faster to complete than target-state design
questions.explain: Skipping current-state analysis is how an architect ends up proposing something impossible, like real-time integration with a system that has never supported it — the target state has to be grounded in what actually exists.

questions.q: Which LTV Global system is described as having no modern API, with batch flat files via SFTP as the only integration path?
options: Meridian ERP
LedgerPoint
Okta
Snowflake
questions.explain: LedgerPoint is the mainframe-based financial system with no modern API at all — batch flat files via SFTP are the only way in or out, a permanent constraint rather than a temporary gap.

questions.q: Which system does this lesson identify as holding EMEA field service history and contact data found nowhere else in the landscape?
options: EuroCRM
Meridian ERP
Snowflake
Okta
questions.explain: EuroCRM is the decade-old EMEA-only CRM holding irreplaceable service history and contact data, which is why Lesson 20's migration strategy has to carry that data forward rather than simply retiring the system and losing it.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what integration style is realistically achievable with Meridian ERP, given its current SOAP and REST endpoints?
options: No integration of any kind is possible
Near-real-time request/response integration
Only batch flat-file transfer, identical to LedgerPoint
Only integration through a retired system like EuroCRM
questions.explain: Unlike LedgerPoint, Meridian ERP exposes SOAP and newer REST endpoints and can support near-real-time request/response integration — it is legacy but not frozen.

questions.q: What does the lesson say about Snowflake's current role at LTV Global before this transformation?
options: It does not exist yet and must be stood up from scratch as part of this project
It already exists as the enterprise data warehouse, but no system currently feeds it reliably or automatically
It is a legacy mainframe system that must be retired
It is the company's identity provider
questions.explain: Snowflake already exists as LTV Global's data warehouse; the problem this project solves is connecting it properly, not standing up a new warehouse from nothing, since no system currently feeds it in a reliable, automated way.
